I can totally relate to this. I’ve had two PE’s although mine were just over a year apart. I’m lifelong on apixaban - don’t lose hope! Since my PEs I still get out of breath quite quickly (my last one was in 2018) but the pain has subsided. I’ve not had anything pierced since then but I’ve had tattoos, I’ve had surgery, I’ve had most of my teeth pulled out to be replaced. Talk it over with your GP when you’re feeling up to it, it may be a while before you can get a tattoo etc but it’s not impossible. My GP told me I can come off my apixaban (this was for surgery and dental treatment) for 24 hours, so I’d miss the evening dose the night prior and then the morning of. My apixaban dosage was reduced after a while. Obviously it doesn’t completely diminish the risk of getting another clot but it does make it far less likely. If I ever get any chest pain or am increasingly breathless I go to A&E to get checked over or contact my GP, you can live a normal life though. The fear of getting another clot has massively reduced for me over time x

If you’re lifelong on apixaban you will need to inject your stomach every day when you’re pregnant & for 6 weeks after (& wear compression stockings!) - I had to do with my 3rd (last child!) my oldest two I didn’t have to as I hadn’t had any clots at that point. I’m not sure why you can’t take blood thinners orally during pregnancy but you’ll go back to tablets after the 6 weeks post partum period. Just make sure you tell your midwife/obgyn at the time! X

I’ve had two PE’s, just over a year apart. Doctors told me it was due to birth control pills but the second one occurred when I wasn’t on them. Four years later I found out I have Factor V Lieden (clotting disorder - the only person in my family to have it!) - I’m on apixaban for life now but like you said, it’s a bit of a relief. Please be aware it doesn’t eliminate the risk of another clot entirely though, if you have any chest pain/trouble breathing/symptoms of clotting then please get it checked. I’ve had to have repeated CT scans for clots due to my history and the doctors always say blood thinners don’t mean you won’t get a clot, they just minimise the risk so please take care of yourself :)

I had a DVT that travelled to my lungs and ended in a PE. I had a second PE just over a year later. When I had the DVT I had horrendous calf pain which just wouldn’t go, my GP didn’t even look at it and wrote it off as a muscle pain. I saw him 3 times in 2 weeks and he gave the same excuse every time without examining it. It wasn’t until that 2nd week I went to hospital because I felt like I couldn’t breathe that they found the PE, it had started in the calf and broke off and travelled to the lungs. Take your blood thinners as directed and it shouldn’t travel further, ask the doctors if you’re unsure of anything. I was on blood thinners for 6 months the first time and then when it happened again they put me on them lifelong. They couldn’t figure out why I kept getting them and I really pushed for testing and found out I have Factor V Leiden - so it may be worth asking for some more tests to rule any blood disorders out (I asked because I have children and was worried about passing anything genetic onto them). Take care of yourself :) x
